topline.text: Another genuinely quiet 24-48 hours - across DfE, Ofsted, safeguarding, funding and Sheffield/South Yorkshire sources, nothing cleared the bar for new, properly corroborated news, so today's edition runs short rather than padded.
One to put on the radar: DfE's accredited statistics release for autumn-term 2025/26 suspensions and permanent exclusions is due this month, with no exact day confirmed yet.
Reminder, not new: DfE's call for evidence on school exclusion reform still closes 19 November - under three weeks away.

diary.text: DfE due to publish autumn 2025/26 suspensions and permanent exclusions statistics for England.
DfE's call for evidence on school exclusion reform (behaviour strategies, in-school units, managed moves) closes.

items.lede: Autumn exclusion stats due this month.
items.body: DfE's accredited statistics announcement confirms the autumn term 2025/26 suspensions and permanent exclusions release - broken down by school type, with reasons - is scheduled for November, though an exact publication day hasn't been set. It'll be the first in-year readout since the 2024/25 full-year figures came out in the summer.
items.action: Worth flagging to the inclusion team as one to watch for this year's AP and exclusions trend once it lands.

box.label: Jargon-buster - managed move
box.intro: Comes up throughout DfE's live exclusion-reform consultation.
box.text: A voluntary, agreed transfer of a pupil to a different mainstream school - with both schools' and the parents' consent - used as an alternative to permanent exclusion. It's one of the behaviour tools DfE's call for evidence (closing 19 Nov) is asking the sector to weigh in on.
